chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the tailor and the goldsmith, are they considered to be carrying the impurity (of the garment)? He said, 'People are not valid (in their prayers) unless they carry the impurity.' And Yunus used to act upon this and accept it.

key_terms.اَلْقَصَّارُ: The tailor (specifically one who washes and mends clothes)
key_terms.يَأْخُذُهُ: He accepted it (as a legal ruling)

ai.seo_question: Are tailors and goldsmiths considered to carry impurity, and does this affect their prayer validity?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that tailors and goldsmiths are exempt from the requirement of removing impurity (najāsah) from items they handle for repair, as their livelihood depends on this practical necessity. This ruling, validated by Yunus ibn Abi al-‘A’la who applied it personally, highlights the Shia legal principle of 'ease in necessity' (al-ḥājah) for artisans, ensuring their prayers remain valid despite incidental contact with impurities during their trade.
